entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed seeking to declare the action of the respondents in taking forcible possession of petitioners residential plots in an extent of Ac.16.6 guntas in Survey Nos.68, 582,
584, 585 to 588, 597, 599, 600, 601, 604 and 605 etc., situated at Mandapalli Village, Siddipet (Urban) Mandal and District, as illegal and arbitrary and for other appropriate reliefs.

2. The petitioners herein claim to be the owners and possessors of different plots of land, in an extent of Ac.16.6 guntas, situated in Survey Nos.68, 582, 584, 585 to 588, 597, 599, 600, 601, 604 and 605 etc., situated at Mandapalli Village, Siddipet (Urban) Mandal and District, having purchased the same by way of various registered sale deeds.

It is the case of the petitioners that respondent No.2 herein issued a Notification under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Act") proposing to acquire land admeasuring Ac.84.00 guntas situated in various survey numbers of Mandapalli Village of Siddipet Urban Mandal and District, for public purpose i.e., to lay a railway line in between Manoharabad - Kottapalli New Broad Guage Railway Line.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Kottapalli New Broad Guage Railway Line
entities.label: GPE

sentences.text:
3. The grievance of the petitioners is that the respondents, without conducting any survey and localisation of the plots purchased by them under various registered sale deeds and without considering social impact assessment study and environmental impact assessment as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (for short "the Act"), under the guise of acquisition, are trying to take forcible possession of their respective plots of land.
4. Learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition has placed before this Court a copy of the written instructions received from respondent No.4 herein i.e., the Revenue Divisional Officer,
Siddipet, wherein it is stated that a preliminary notification has been published to an extent of Ac.50.29 in Form-IV under Section 11(1) of the Act for construction of New Broad-Gauge Railway line; gram sabha was also conducted in Mandapally Village on 17.03.2018 under Section 11(2) of the Act and no objections were received in stipulated period; later on, a declaration was published under Section 19(1) of the Act in District Gazette No.736/2019 dated 20.01.2020, intending to acquire an extent of Ac.26.22 gutnas of patta land; in this regard, out of the total extent of Ac.50.29 guntas,
consent was given to an extent of Ac.42.01 guntas and accordingly compensation was paid and for the remaining extent of Ac.8.27 guntas of land, since it has been found that the pattadars and occupants are different, a general award was passed; and as such compensation amount was deposited before the R & R Authority in the year 2021 for payment of the same to the awardees.
5. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioners that even though the subject lands have been purchased by them under various registered sale deeds, the respondents without conducting any survey and localisation of the land required for acquisition and without mentioning all the names of the land owners whose lands are affected in the notification, but by irregularly showing the name of their vendor, are trying to take forcible possession of their respective plots.

7. In view of the same, the writ petition is disposed of by permitting the petitioners to submit all the relevant documents, which establish their ownership in respect of the subject land, before the respondents, who in turn shall conduct survey basing on the said documents, and if it is found that the petitioners' lands are affected in the acquisition, the respondents shall pay compensation to the petitioners, in accordance with the provisions of the Act, and in the event if it is found that the petitioners' lands are not affected in the acquisition, the respondents shall not interfere with the possession of the petitioners over the subject lands in any manner nor prevent them from entering into the subject lands.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

C.V.BHASKAR REDDY, J 12.09.2024 JSU T.S.Padmalatha vs The State Of Telangana on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139695178/
